'''''Urtica thunbergiana''''', also known as the '''Japanese nettle''' or '''hairy nettle''', is a [[species]] of perennial herbs in the family [[Urticaceae]].<ref>{{ Cite web |url = https://tai2.ntu.edu.tw/species/310%20021%2002%200 |title = Urtica thunbergiana 蕁麻 Urtica thunbergiana Sieb. & Zucc.|publisher = 國立台灣大學生態學與演化生物學研究所 |language = en |accessdate = 2022-12-06}}</ref><ref name="Flora of China">{{ Cite web |url = http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242353638 |title = 咬人荨麻 yao ren qian ma Urtica macrorrhiza Handel-Mazzetti. |publisher = Flora of China @ efloras.org |language = en |accessdate = 2022-12-06}}</ref> It is found in Japan, China and Taiwan. The habitat of the species is moist forests in the mountains. It is in flower from July to September, and its seeds ripen from August to October. The [[larva]]e of ''[[Vanessa indica]]'', a species of butterfly, are known to feed on ''U. thunbergiana''.

Chinese common names for ''U. thunbergiana'' translate to "biting cat", "biting nettle", and "stinging herbs" due to the stinging hairs on the plant that can cause skin pain, redness, burning or itching.<ref name=林育安>{{ Cite web |url = https://kmweb.coa.gov.tw/theme_data.php?theme=news&sub_theme=agri_life&id=55030 |title = 有毒植物－全植株布滿有毒焮毛的咬人貓 |author = 林育安 |publisher = 行政院農業委員會 |language = zh |accessdate = 2022-12-05}}</ref> Usually, the stinging sensation lasts for about 2 to 4 hours, and some people even feel the pain for 1 to 2 days, depending on the individual's constitution.<ref name=林育安/><ref name=咬人貓>{{Cite web |url = https://www1.ncyu.edu.tw/newsite/bulletin.aspx?bulletin_sn=33792 |title = 「咬人貓」不咬人 去毒酥炸變風味野菜 |date = 31 May 2017 |publisher = National Chiayi University |language = zh |accessdate = 2022-12-06 |archive-date = 2022-12-06 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221206090252/https://www1.ncyu.edu.tw/newsite/bulletin.aspx?bulletin_sn=33792 |url-status = dead }}</ref>

As with other species in the genus, ''U. thunbergiana'' can also be used as a food ingredient, because boiling water can destroy its toxicity.<ref name=咬人貓/> In Taiwan, in addition to flavored soup,<ref>{{ Cite web |url = http://het-vl.com.tw/node/844 |title = 有毒植物系列–咬人貓 |publisher = Health e talk |language = zh |accessdate = 2022-12-06}}</ref> it is also made into flavored bread,<ref>{{ Cite web |url = https://news.tvbs.com.tw/life/46396 |title = 毒刺「咬人貓」 高溫水煮製麵包可食 |publisher = TVBS新聞網 |language = zh |accessdate = 2022-12-06}}</ref> Chinese [[shortbread]] or crispy fried leaves.<ref name=咬人貓/>

From 2016 to 2017, [[Shei-Pa National Park]]'s headquarters commissioned a survey of animals along the [[Mount Dabajian]] hiking trail. In this investigation, a video of a [[Taiwan serow]] feeding on ''U. thunbergiana'' was recorded.<ref>{{ Cite web |url = https://e-info.org.tw/node/209918 |title = 台灣野山羊大啖咬人貓 珍貴影像紀錄曝光 |publisher = Environmental Information Center|language = zh |accessdate = 2022-12-06}}</ref>
